A significant group difference was found in suppression-induced forgetting, as revealed by a significant condition-by-group interaction, F(1, 30) = 7.556, p = .010, ηp² = .201.

This interaction was driven by a significant inversion of suppression-induced forgetting in the PTSD group (i.e., better memory performance for suppress items compared with baseline items; M = -5.2%), F(1, 15) = 5.288, p = .036, ηp² = .261 (Bayes factor favoring the alternative hypothesis = 2.09), in the absence of significant suppression in the control group (M = 3.5%, n.s.).
